prompt: Hi, I'm Sarah from Finance. We're replacing our old emailed spreadsheet expense process with a proper system. I've put all the relevant documents in this folder – policy excerpts, last year's claims data, meeting notes, audit findings, vendor info. Could you read through it all and draft a requirements document for the new system? Focus on what it must do, not how to build it. We need something to give to vendors. Put the output in docs/requirements.md. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}.

facts.answer: For claims over £1,000, we need a second approver from Finance even if the first approver is at the right level. The Head of Finance can be the second approver for any claim over £1,000.
Managers can approve their own expenses up to £100 without needing another approver. Over £100, it goes to their line manager or the Head of Finance if they have no line manager.
Photos of receipts are acceptable for all claims, but they must show the date, amount, vendor, and items clearly. Blurry photos or cropped receipts need to be resubmitted.

The grant renewals changed the caps from April: the Youth Empowerment Programme grant now has a £60 daily subsistence limit per person. The Community Engagement Programme allows £95 per night for accommodation and no more than £35 daily for food.

We run payments twice a month: on the 10th for claims approved by the 25th of previous month, and on the 25th for claims approved by the 10th of current month. Miss those cutoffs and payment waits for next cycle.

When a line manager is away, their deputy approves claims. If no deputy, it goes to the department head. For Head of Finance absence, the Executive Director covers. All delegation must be set up in the system in advance.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const d=fs.readFileSync("docs/requirements.md","utf8"); const m=/```json\n([\s\S]*?)\n```/.exec(d); if(!m) process.exit(1); const j=JSON.parse(m[1]); if(!Array.isArray(j.requirements)||j.requirements.length<5) process.exit(1); if(!j.requirements.every(r=>r.id&&r.text)) process.exit(1);'

rubric.criterion: Requirements are actionable for a vendor, not just problem statements. Fail: requirements describe the old spreadsheet problems, or say 'the system should support approvals' with no limits. Partial: some requirements have limits, but several of these are missing or vague: a second Finance approver over £1,000, self-approval up to £100 with a line manager or the Head of Finance above that, the 30-day submission deadline, 7-year record retention, clear photos of receipts accepted with the date, amount, vendor and items visible, payment runs on the 10th and 25th with their cut-offs. Pass: each of these appears as its own testable requirement with the figure, the approver rule (deputy, then escalation when the line manager is away) and the cut-off dates, written as what the system must do and not how to build it. (code cannot check this because it requires judgement about whether requirements specify measurable behaviours rather than just describing current problems)

Document shows understanding of charity-specific constraints like grant compliance and audit requirements. Fail: it reads as a generic expense system with no grant codes or audit trail. Partial: it mentions grants or audits, but not the current rules (grant code validation, the Youth Empowerment Programme limit of £60 daily subsistence per person, the Community Engagement Programme limits of £95 per night for accommodation and £35 daily for food). Pass: it requires grant code validation against each grant's limits as changed from April, an audit trail of every approval, retention for audit, and reporting by grant, and ties each to the audit findings or grant terms in the folder. (code cannot check this because it requires recognising charity context beyond generic expense system features)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the grant caps and approver rules the folder leaves unclear stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the grant caps and approver rules the folder leaves unclear. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the grant caps and approver rules the folder leaves unclear still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

Topics widened in the fix round and trimmed by the lead (overbroad words such as second, self, paid removed).

All 6 facts have natural topics for asking (second approver, self approve, digital receipts, grant daily limit, payment dates, delegation). Each addresses a gap the fixture hints at but doesn't specify. Reference passes all 13 hidden tests.

Fixture contains partial information and hints but NOT the exact scripted facts (no £1,000 threshold, no £100 self-approval, no 10th/25th payment dates stated anywhere). Prompt explicitly says requirements 'must not contain any of the facts'.
